defaults.permitted_development: A garden room can be permitted development in Wales where it remains an incidental garden building, stays within the national outbuilding siting and height limits and is not used as separate living accommodation.

rules.height_rules: Maximum height is 4m for a dual-pitched roof, 3m for a single-pitch or other roof form and 2.5m for a flat roof. Eaves should not exceed 2.5m, and any part within 2m of a boundary should not exceed 2.5m in height.
rules.depth_rules: There is no separate garden-room depth allowance. The key tests are whether the room stays within the curtilage, remains behind the principal elevation and keeps total coverage by additions and outbuildings within 50% of the curtilage excluding the original house.
rules.boundary_rules: The room should stay behind the principal elevation and not project beyond the side elevation where that would bring it closer to a highway than the house, or within 5m of the highway, whichever is nearer. Any part within 2m of a boundary should stay at or below 2.5m, and any part within 2m of the house should stay at or below 1.5m.
rules.roof_rules: The safest Welsh route is a modest single-storey room. Roof form controls the allowed height directly, and balconies, verandas or raised platforms above 300mm are outside the ordinary outbuilding right.
rules.materials_rules: Keep the room clearly ancillary to the house. Modern glazing and cladding can work, but the room should not be fitted out or used as a self-contained bedroom, bathroom and kitchen suite.

rules.permitted_development: In Wales, a modest garden room can often use the outbuilding permitted development rules if it stays incidental to the house, remains behind the principal elevation and complies with the national size and height limits. It should not function as a self-contained annexe.

rules.height_rules: Use the Welsh outbuilding height limits: up to 4m overall with more than one roof pitch, up to 3m with a single-pitch or other roof form, and up to 2.5m with a flat roof. Eaves should stay at or below 2.5m, and boundary siting within 2m also triggers a 2.5m cap.
rules.depth_rules: Garden rooms in Wales are not governed by a standalone depth figure. What matters is curtilage location, staying behind the principal elevation and not pushing total coverage by additions and outbuildings beyond the normal 50% allowance.
rules.boundary_rules: Boundary and highway siting are crucial for a Welsh garden room. Keep it behind the principal elevation, avoid side positions that come nearer to the highway than the house or within 5m of it, limit anything within 2m of a boundary to 2.5m overall and keep any part within 2m of the house to 1.5m high.
rules.roof_rules: Keep the garden room single storey with a simple roof. The roof type determines the height cap, and raised platforms, balconies or veranda-style designs above 300mm need separate planning assessment.
rules.materials_rules: The finish can be contemporary, but the room should still read as an ancillary domestic structure tied to the house. Avoid layouts, servicing or everyday use that turn it into self-contained accommodation.

restrictions.conservation_area: In Wales, conservation area controls and any Article 4 direction can remove normal householder permitted development rights for visible external work. Check the planning register before relying on national allowances.
restrictions.listed_building: Listed building consent may be needed for internal or external works that affect the character of a listed building or its curtilage structures. Minor-looking changes can still need consent in Wales.
restrictions.article4_notes: No borough-wide Article 4 note is recorded here, but site-specific directions or planning conditions can still remove permitted development rights on particular properties.

rules.permitted_development: Welsh permitted development can often cover a garden room used as a home office, studio or similar ancillary space, provided it stays within the outbuilding rules and does not become separate living accommodation.

rules.materials_rules: Materials do not need to copy the house exactly, but the room should remain subordinate in appearance and incidental in use rather than operating as a separate annexe.

rules.boundary_rules: The hardest checks are usually siting and proximity. rules.height_rules: Maximum height is 4m for a dual-pitched roof, 3m for a single-pitch or other roof form and 2.5m for a flat roof. Eaves should not exceed 2.5m, and any part within 2m of a boundary should not exceed 2.5m in height.
